html:
Ahmad Shah Durrani founded the Durrani Empire in 1747 and is often called the founder of modern Afghanistan.

A young Pashtun of the Abdali tribe, he rose as a cavalry commander under Nader Shah of Persia. When Nader Shah was murdered in 1747, a council of tribal chiefs near Kandahar chose Ahmad as their king, and he took the name Durr-i Durran, "pearl of pearls".

He spent the next twenty-five years at war. He took Khorasan in the west and much of what is now Pakistan, and invaded India many times, taking the wealth of the weakened Mughal Empire and sacking Delhi in 1757. In 1761 he crushed the Marathas at the Third Battle of Panipat, one of the bloodiest battles of the century. Afghans still call him Ahmad Shah Baba, "the father".
